findings.claim: The origin accepts and stores an applied peer receipt without verifying the receipt signature against the enrolled target key.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 2.3 requires "verified per-peer receipt return" and the design states "Returned peer receipts are verified against the enrolled key and stored before aggregate terminal publication," but `RemoteOrigin::dispatch` only calls `verify_peer_response(&response, &dispatch, &self.enrollment)?` and then persists `response.receipt` via `self.queue.transition(... response.state, response.run_id, response.receipt, ...)`; `verify_peer_response` in `substrate/exec-remote/src/crypto.rs` verifies the signed peer response envelope, while receipt verification is only implemented in `RemoteTarget::verify_target_receipt`, so an enrolled peer can sign an envelope containing an invalid or differently signed receipt that the origin records as applied.
findings.suggested_fix: Before transitioning to `Applied` in `RemoteOrigin::dispatch`, when `response.receipt` is present, load the target enrollment binding, construct a `VerificationKey`, call `verify_receipt(&receipt, &key, Some(&dispatch.request), None)`, and reject the response unless it is valid; add a regression with a valid peer-response signature carrying an invalid receipt signature.
